question: to the Commission Regina Doherty (PPE) Subject:
What flexibility do Member States have under existing EU law to use VAT and other fiscal measures to reduce the cost of newly constructed housing for first-time buyers?

Can the Commission clarify whether Directive 2006/112/EC1, as amended by Directive (EU) 2022/542, permits a Member State to apply a reduced VAT rate of 9 % to the supply or construction of new residential properties where the property is purchased by a first-time buyer as their principal private residence, whether such a reduced rate may be targeted specifically at first-time buyers and/or owner-occupiers, rather than applying to all purchasers of new residential property, and whether a targeted VAT reduction of this nature, together with an exemption from residential stamp duty and a reduction in or cap on development contributions, would raise concerns under EU State aid rules?
Council Directive 2006/112/EC of 28 November 2006 on the common system of value added tax, (OJ L 347, 11.12.2006, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2006/112/oj). 1
